newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI says to appeal pesticide decision.
newsitem.headline: ICI says to appeal pesticide decision.

text.p: Chemicals group ICI Australia Ltd said on Tuesday it would appeal against a Federal Court decision that it was negligent for some claims in a class action relating to the pesticide Helix.

The Federal Court found earlier that ICI had in some cases breached its duty of care over the manufacture and distribution of the pesticide, which cattle producers from New South Wales and Queensland alleged contaminated their stock.
More than 450 producers are seeking over A$100 million in compensation following the discovery of chemical residue in cattle fed cotton trash sprayed with Helix during drought between 1989 to 1994.
The discovery led to a beef contamination scare and a temporary freeze on some exports, which the producers said cost them both domestic and export sales.
ICI said in a statement it believed responsibility for the economic losses lay elsewhere.
The company said it had complied with regulatory requirements and industry standards when it registered Helix for use on cotton crops.
It was not aware of the practice of feeding cotton trash to cattle, and the practice was not widespread before the extreme drought of the 1990s, the statement said.
Cattle producers' solicitor Peter Long said the ruling had ramifications for the way chemical companies marketed and developed their products.

"It certainly puts back on to the chemical companies a much more stringent obligation to review the research that they do (and) the surveillance and monitoring, particularly after the chemical is released," he told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.
The New South Wales Farmers' Association called for a detailed review of the procedures used in registering Helix.
The court dismissed negligence claims brought against the state governments of New South Wales and Queensland.
An out-of-court settlement offer by ICI was rejected last week by producers, who said it was insufficient and unworkable.
